speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the UN Climate Change Conference 2023 (COP28), Singapore co-facilitated negotiations on mitigation and the first global stocktake that contributed to the successful adoption of the UAE Consensus.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As part of our Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy (LEDS), Singapore has committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, despite being a small, alternative energy disadvantaged city state with many natural limitations on our climate action measures.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our LEDS is aligned with the UAE Consensus.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Over the past few years, many Members have spoken extensively about the urgent need to address climate change – in particular, during the two climate Motions that have been endorsed by this House, as well as the debate on the Carbon Pricing (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our carbon tax ensures that the negative externalities of carbon emissions are properly priced, and is an effective mechanism to spur economy-wide decarbonisation efforts to achieve our net-zero ambition.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At COP28, Singapore signed on to the Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency pledge, which is a collective global effort that aims to triple the world's renewable energy generation capacity and double annual energy efficiency by 2030.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We aim to at least double this deployment again, to achieve our target of at least 2,000 MWp by 2030.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are also partnering like-minded countries to import low-carbon electricity from the region.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When implemented by 2035, these projects will meet about 30% of our electricity needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They will also support our neighbours' development of renewable energy projects and serve as building blocks towards our shared vision of an ASEAN Power Grid.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Beyond solar power and electricity imports, we will need to leverage other energy alternatives to further expand our low-carbon energy capacity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are working closely with the industry and academia to realise the potential of low-carbon technologies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These include research and development as well as industry projects in areas such as innovative solar power deployment, transport and utilisation of hydrogen and ammonia, carbon capture, utilisation and storage, as well as advanced geothermal energy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Government is progressively updating our regulations to facilitate the adoption of these low-carbon alternatives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) announced new emissions standards for power generation units, which will require all new generation units to be at least 30% hydrogen-ready by volume, with the ability to be retrofitted to become 100% hydrogen-ready in the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the area of energy efficiency, Singapore's overall energy efficiency is already much better than the global average.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: According to the International Energy Agency, Singapore's energy intensity in 2019 was almost half that of global energy intensity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This has been achieved through consistent efforts to identify and realise energy efficiency opportunities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, the National Environment Agency (NEA) enhanced the Energy Conservation Act in 2017 to require energy-intensive industrial facilities to conduct regular energy efficiency assessments.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Another example is the Economic Development Board (EDB)'s Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions, which supports businesses in improving their energy efficiency and reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For households, our Climate Friendly Households Programme continues to help eligible households offset the higher cost of energy-efficient appliances.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Accelerating the energy transition in Singapore will require a whole-of-nation effort.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Government, businesses, communities and individuals must all contribute to this overall goal.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Even so, no country can tackle climate change alone.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Despite our natural limitations in size and natural resources, Singapore is committed to do our part as a responsible global citizen and will continue to work with like-minded countries and companies for a cleaner, greener future.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My first question is, as the Minister was at COP28, I would like to hear from her whether she is satisfied with the overall outcomes of COP28.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second question is about this call to triple renewable energy capacity and doubling the rate of efficiency by 2030.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is a major undertaking, notwithstanding the plans we have in place.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My third question is, in COP28, there were also increasing calls for the use of nuclear energy as one of the renewable sources, with the goal to triple nuclear energy capacity by 2050.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I believe there were 20-over countries that came up with a declaration, including the United States (US) and some Asian countries like Japan and Korea.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Minister whether this declaration will have any bearing on the Government's position on nuclear energy as another source of renewable energy?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is being held in a period where there is high energy inflation, there is also great geopolitical contention.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But the fact that all parties were able to come together and again, re-affirm that the UN Climate Change Conference (COP) is the only relevant multilateral platform for climate discussion and negotiations is a major undertaking.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On top of that, I think there were several improvements and I would say movements in negotiations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Climate projections, temperatures are telling us that we need to do more in the near term.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The focus of the global stocktake has been a lot on implementation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: What the Member has spoken about – whether it is three times renewable energy capacity, two times on energy efficiency improvements – these are going into the so-called "nitty gritty".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is no longer just setting net-zero targets, but, really, what is the pathway to 1.5 °C.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There were some very specific recommendations and agreements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think that is a major achievement of COP28.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is a very extensive and comprehensive process, and it does not do justice to the process by just answering supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having said that, I think it is important and useful for Members to also understand that this being a global UN process, we need to pay attention to the language that is being used.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Although there is a consensus, the basis of the consensus is still on the basis of the Paris Agreement, where some of the basic values – for example, common but differentiated responsibilities, nationally determined contributions (NDCs), national context – are still relevant.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The implementation is still dependent on countries incorporating those into their NDCs, taking into consideration their own national context.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On nuclear energy, that is the same basis.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A few countries have a declaration, they have started to look at it separately.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These declarations outside the negotiation documents are helpful.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Because these are the initiatives that are pushing movements, directions and developments in technologies, in finance and in global action.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we need to look at it in two ways: look at what is happening outside the negotiations, look at what is in the documents and see how Singapore can leverage on some of the developments, such as the development of technology in nuclear energy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is an area where we have some interest to understand the development, because we think that the advanced nuclear technology offers us some potential.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In terms of safety, there is better safety in these technologies, and also, in terms of cost competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first, following up to the previous supplementary question and in relation to my original Parliamentary Question, given that this is the goal that we have, is there any timetable or transitional plan or milestones that we will be setting along the way in order to achieve this in the next couple of decades or so.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second supplementary question is, the Minister also mentioned at COP28 that we will not be claiming from the Loss and Damage (L&D) Fund.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I just wanted to understand whether or not we will be contributing to the L&D Fund today or any time in the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think I have gone into some extent on how we are progressing on our climate action.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In fact, from the Singapore Green Plan that was announced in 2021, we have been updating some of the sub-goals almost annually.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Even though there are five pillars and two horizontals, there have been movements on every vertical, every pillar of work that we are doing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I would encourage the Member to watch this space, to give us suggestions as to how we can move further.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And I think the Member has the assurance that all the participating Ministries are working flat out towards our net-zero 2050 goals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is by no means easy, given our constraints.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In fact, we are looking at some of the alternatives that have yet to come on stream, such as low-carbon hydrogen that is so important in our energy transition but which we are still in the process of developing a viable, commercial market for it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, do not misunderstand that although there is a lot of effort, there are also many, many challenges.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we are not afraid of challenges, and we will do our very best for climate action and for Singapore's decarbonisation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On L&D, can I understand from the Member whether it is the Workers' Party's position that Singapore should contribute and, if so, what would the Member suggest that we contribute?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think there was also a related supplementary question that was asked last year.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I know that the Minister mentioned that we will be facilitating countries to claim from the L&D fund.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But at the same time, in light of what was also shared by my fellow colleague, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, about contributions to international funds and all that, I think we do have a role to play in terms of — we may not be the main contributors to this from the historical context, but I do believe that we do have a part to play in terms of using finance terms, introducing, say, seed funding, to enable people to join in the cause and to show people that, look, even though Singapore is small and resource-constrained, we are also doing our part in that regard.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I did not get a clear question from the Member because the Workers' Party has been asking us: are we contributing to L&D?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I just wanted to know whether the Member is asking us to contribute to the L&D funds specifically.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think that our position is quite aligned, that we will do our part in finance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It has a specific purpose – loss and damage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is where I think countries that are looking to claim are looking for outright grants.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we believe that we can play a role to facilitate, to develop capabilities, to do technological transfers, and capability and capacity-building.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But if the Member would like to suggest a sum to the Government to contribute to L&D, I would really welcome his suggestion.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My first supplementary question is that Singapore set up the Singapore Pavilion at COP28.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Could the Minister share what were the objectives behind the Pavilion and also the cost and resources that were involved in setting up the Pavilion?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And how does the Government assess the gains that we have made through the Pavilion and the efforts of our delegation at COP28 in contributing to the agenda and objectives of COP28?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There is some time for us to do it, until the end of this year.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I think we are making good progress.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Unabated coal, fossil fuel subsidies, as I mentioned in my reply, our LEDS is actually aligned to the UAE Consensus.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we do not think we need to make major adjustments because it is out of sync or out of place with what has been agreed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we will, basically, progress with what we have already planned under the Singapore Green Plan.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In particular, can I ask the Minister, given the speed of developments in the climate space, including what commentators described as the risk of a climate endgame with catastrophic change upon the world, will Singapore – at a whole-of-Government level – look at moving ahead of the market in certain strategic areas?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Two years ago, I had asked about Singapore and a potential position as a hydrogen hub.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The Minister mentioned this in her earlier answers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask: is there a role for us more actively moving ahead of the market in a calibrated way so that we can be the first mover and not last mover or too late to move when the market finally evolves.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, I think this is where our Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) and Ministry of Transport (MOT) folks are working flat out to be ahead but, at the same time, leveraging on the massive investments in R&D that is going into new areas.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The world is looking for new solutions – solutions in hydrogen and carbon capture, for example, are not an exclusive arena for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And given the kind of resources that are available globally, it will serve Singapore's interest to really tap on and leverage on such global investments.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the maritime sector, for example, we are also pioneering, with other ports, green shipping with alternative fuels, learning how to handle, store and move new types of fuels.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we are moving in many, many different ways.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Even in aviation, a similar undertaking is ongoing to really be at the cusp of change.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will not be alone and we want to really be out there, to be early enough to tap the change and not to be left behind, but at the same time, also capture opportunities that may arise.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Regarding my third supplementary question, yes, I did hear the Minister in her original answer.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: This is regarding the transition efforts from fossil fuel, including unabated coal power, reducing methane emissions and phasing out inefficient fuel subsidies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My supplementary question pertains to us living in an area where our neighbouring countries may use a lot of coal, for example.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, I am asking how Singapore can engage our neighbours or other countries globally by action and words to persuade other countries to journey along this transition as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will try to do our best by being, I would say, an active partner in global negotiations, as well as propagating, advocating at the regional level.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, whether it is at ASEAN or other regional groupings, we will do our best.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, we bring our climate projections, the 3rd National Climate Change Study (V3), to many of the ASEAN fora, whether it is on agriculture, environment or water.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is why I think the UNFCCC remains such an important multilateral forum for us to have those discussions on the global basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think various sectors have just released their refreshed ITMs 2025.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: ITMs do not come under the purview of MSE per se.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We do have ITMs that are under MSE that have to do with environmental services and waste management.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But I will bring that as a suggestion to my colleagues who are responsible for the respective ITMs.
